intro: Look around the room you are in. The floor covers a certain area. The walls need a certain amount of paint. The air inside fills a certain volume. The corners of the door are square, the beams above you meet at angles someone had to measure, and if you drew the whole room on paper you would need a scale. Geometry is the mathematics of space, and it began with people who needed to build things and measure land.

This unit has three chapters. The first measures flat shapes and solid ones: the area of triangles, trapezoids and circles, the surface area of boxes and pyramids, and the volume of prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres. Every formula comes from cutting a shape apart and rearranging it into something simpler. The second chapter is about angles: what happens when lines cross, when a line cuts across two parallel lines, and why the angles of a triangle always add to 180 degrees. It ends with scale drawings, the tool that lets a floor plan stand in for a building.

The third chapter moves shapes around the coordinate plane by sliding, flipping, turning and stretching them, and asks what stays the same. Then it proves one of the most famous facts in all of mathematics, the Pythagorean theorem, and uses it to find distances no ruler can reach. By the end you will be able to measure a circle with a string, check a corner with a rope, and find how far a drone flies from one map point to another.
bigQuestion: How can a few facts about shapes let us measure space, check a corner and find a distance we cannot walk?

timeline.t: Babylonian clay tablets list whole-number sides of right triangles, like 3, 4 and 5
An Egyptian scroll, the Rhind papyrus, shows methods for finding the area of fields and the volume of granaries
Pythagoras and his followers in Greece study the right-triangle rule that now carries his name
Euclid's Elements gathers geometry into definitions, axioms and proofs, including the Pythagorean theorem
Archimedes traps π between 3 10/71 and 3 1/7 and finds the volume of a sphere inside its cylinder
Eratosthenes uses shadow angles and parallel sun rays to estimate the circumference of the Earth
Fibonacci's books bring Hindu-Arabic numerals and practical geometry to European merchants
Descartes links algebra and geometry with coordinates, so shapes can be described by equations
Surveyors cross the United States with chains and angle-measuring instruments, laying out townships and city grids
Engineers use scale drawings and blueprints to design skyscrapers, bridges and highways
Phones and satellites use coordinates and distance formulas to map and navigate the world

words.d: the amount of flat space a shape covers, measured in square units
the total area of all the faces of a solid
the amount of space inside a solid, measured in cubic units
the number, about 3.14, that a circle's circumference is divided by its diameter
a flat pattern that folds up into a solid
two angles that add to 180 degrees
a line that crosses two or more other lines, making matching angles when those lines are parallel
any two sides of a triangle must add to more than the third side
the number every length is multiplied by in a scaled copy; area is multiplied by its square
the same shape and size; rigid motions carry one onto the other
the same shape, possibly a different size; rigid motions plus a dilation carry one onto the other
the longest side of a right triangle, across from the right angle; a² + b² = c²

test.q: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
A triangle has base 12 m and height 7 m. What is its area?
A trapezoid has bases 4 cm and 10 cm and height 3 cm. What is its area?
A circle has diameter 8 in. About what is its area?
test.why: Radius 4, so 3.14 × 4² = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 in². 25.12 is the circumference.

test.q: A box is 6 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm. What is its surface area?
A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. About what is its volume?
test.why: 3.14 × 3² × 5 = 3.14 × 9 × 5 = 141.3 cm³. 47.1 is a cone of the same size.

test.q: A sphere has radius 2 cm. About what is its volume?
An angle measures 58 degrees. What is its supplement?
A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 40 degrees. What is its alternate interior angle?
test.why: Alternate interior angles between parallel lines are equal, so 40 degrees.

test.q: Two angles of a triangle are 52 and 71 degrees. What is the third?
A drawing uses a scale of 1 cm : 5 m. A room is 4.5 cm long on the drawing. How long is the real room?
test.why: Drawing to real means multiply: 4.5 × 5 = 22.5 m.

test.q: The point (1, −4) is reflected across the x-axis. Where is its image?
test.why: A flip across the horizontal axis changes the sign of y only: (1, 4).

test.q: The point (3, 2) is dilated from the origin with scale factor 4. Where is its image?
A right triangle has legs 7 and 24. What is the hypotenuse?
What is the distance between (0, 3) and (6, 11)?

write.prompt: A rectangular fish tank is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm tall. Find how much water fills it, and how much glass it takes to build it with no top. Then a friend says a 70-cm rod will lie flat on the bottom, corner to corner. Find the diagonal of the bottom to decide if that is true. Explain every step.
tips: State each answer clearly with its unit: cubic centimeters for water, square centimeters for glass.
For the glass, list every face you counted and say which face you left out and why.
For the rod, name the two legs and the hypotenuse before you square anything.
Check each result a second way, such as putting the three sides back into a² + b² = c².
Say in one sentence why volume and surface area answer different questions.
